summary.title: Build an Appointment Scheduler Using React, Twilio and Cosmic JS
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a React appointment scheduler with Material UI, an Express backend, Twilio confirmation texts, and a Cosmic JS CMS data store and extension.
takeaways: Model appointments and site configs as Cosmic JS object types with metafields.
Set up a React + Webpack + Babel project with Material UI components.
Structure app state and methods for a three-step scheduling flow (date, time slot, contact info).
Use an Express backend as a middleman so the Cosmic bucket keys stay out of the frontend.
The tutorial plans to send Twilio confirmation texts and build a Cosmic JS extension to manage appointments (the excerpt ends before these parts).
summary.summary: This tutorial walks through building an appointment scheduler where users pick a day and a one-hour slot between 9AM and 5PM. Data lives in Cosmic JS, an API-first CMS, with Appointments and Configs object types. The React front end uses Webpack, Babel and Material UI, and reads data through a small Express backend that also calls Twilio for confirmation texts. The excerpt covers the setup, state design, method planning, view construction, and data fetching and processing; the Twilio integration and Cosmic extension are described in the overview but not shown in the text provided.
